answer: Continuous verifiable delay functions resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to chain sequential modular squarings from epoch randomness and its key, publishing a succinct liveness signal before bidding on tasks like ferrous assays on a knoll. Because each identity needs a dedicated, non-parallelizable execution path, attackers incur linear compute time and energy costs per clone. Still, actors with large processor fleets can run many identities whenever payouts exceed running costs.
